steps.what: Discuss athlete needs and recommend special diets or refer within professional scope

tasks.design: Keep nutrition discussion and scope decisions with the trainer. Existing guidance in {DOCS} supports advice; specialist dietary care remains with the appropriately qualified professional.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nutrition needs depend on individual circumstances rather than a stated performance goal alone.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated automatic dietary recommendation or separate administrative share is established here.
tasks.still_hard: Health, weight and performance concerns may require specialist assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a request falls outside the trainer's competence and explain the referral.
tasks.altitude: Advice boundaries and athlete contact time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: What context a qualified nutrition professional needs

evidence.claim: Nutrition advice requires individual assessment and professional scope awareness; the design establishes no automatic diet-selection saving.

assumptions: Boundary is trainer advice or referral, excluding specialist dietary assessment, prescription and ongoing clinical care. National professional scope must be confirmed locally.

Athletes provide goals and circumstances during s1; clinicians supply applicable guidance before advice where relevant. The trainer verifies and clarifies within the retained time; no free suitable-diet or medically-cleared flag is assumed.
Native guidance access precedes custom code. No new tool or transferred work is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual delegated nutrition scope and referral arrangements
research_questions: Which nutrition requests require a qualified specialist rather than trainer advice?

already_counted.description: Individual discussion, scope assessment and advice or referral

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0 and net=0. Individual advice and scope assessment retain their time.

steps.what: Verify athlete insurance claim sources, disclosure permission and required fields
Prepare the athlete insurance claim form and specified attachments
Check and file the claim, then communicate with insurance providers about queries

tasks.design: Configure claim form assembly in {OTHER}, the insurance claim system, from trainer-verified inputs and selected records in {DOCS}. The trainer checks and files each exact package and retains insurer communication; no coverage decision or diagnostic coding is inferred.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified identity and service facts were copied into insurer-specific forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed field mappings can prefill a supported form from an explicit claim input.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage disputes, missing documentation and disclosure limits require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize what evidence the claim actually supports and communicate unresolved issues accurately.
tasks.altitude: Less claim form copying; disclosure and submission responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How to distinguish a missing field from a disputed claim decision

evidence.claim: Fixed claim fields and selected attachments can be assembled deterministically; insurer compatibility and local labour savings remain an E1 scenario.
GDPR Article 9 concerns health data, which is relevant to access and disclosure for athlete claim records.

assumptions: Boundary is trainer claim preparation, submission and communication, excluding original clinical documentation, insurer adjudication and athlete consent production. Those parties retain existing work; no additional form-filling is transferred to them.

The athlete supplies the claim request and permission evidence, clinicians supply completed care records and the insurer supplies its current form before s1. In s1 the trainer captures athlete/policy IDs, service dates, provider details, amounts/currency, existing authorized codes, attachment versions, recipient and disclosure scope. Its 35 hours include manual transcription, source verification and missing-field clarification. Missing or incompatible fields use manual form completion; no free covered-treatment or disclosure-cleared flag is assumed.

Insurer receipts and queries arise after filing within s3 before query responses and capture; all trainer communication time remains in its 35 hours. Test native claim templates before custom code. OTHER means insurance claim system in every step; unsupported portals remain manual.
unknowns: Insurer form compatibility and actual preparation time
Trainer authority to disclose and submit health records
research_questions: How much form assembly time remains after permission checks, attachment selection and insurer queries are counted?

Exact claim acceptance, filing and insurer communication

incremental.description: Insurer form mappings and failed assembly upkeep
Claim system access and template support

approvals.approved_version: Exact athlete, policy, service fields, codes, amounts, attachment versions, disclosure scope and recipient filed; changed package or query response requires renewed approval.

steps.what: Teach sports medicine courses to athletic training students through explanation and demonstration

tasks.design: Retain course teaching and practical demonstration with the trainer. Materials in {LMS} support the session; no separate material-production or marking baseline is established by this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Students need responsive explanation and observation of their understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability establishes a reduction in direct sports medicine teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Apparent understanding may fail when a learner applies the concept or technique.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize misconceptions and connect theory with observed practice.
tasks.altitude: Teaching and student contact remain unchanged.

reach.task: Demonstrate a practical clinical skill to a learner
reach.learn: How to observe understanding rather than assume it

evidence.claim: Responsive teaching and practical demonstration retain human time; no independent administrative saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is course delivery, excluding material production, grading and general instruction assigned to 4233. A roll-up assigns overlapping teaching once.

The responsible instructor supplies objectives and verified materials before s1. Students supply questions and demonstrated responses during s1 before clarification concludes. Observation and checking remain within its full time; no free competent-student flag is assumed.
Native material access precedes code. No new service is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Course delivery and practical demonstration responsibilities
research_questions: Which learning difficulties require direct demonstration and observation?

steps.what: Perform team support duties including errands, equipment maintenance and stocking supplies

tasks.enabler_now: No new capability removes those physical actions under this task boundary.

tasks.human_edge: Notice damaged, unsuitable or missing supplies and resolve the physical issue.

evidence.claim: Physical maintenance, errands and stocking retain human work; no distinct inventory calculation baseline is established.

Native existing stock tools precede code if a ledger burden is later measured. No new service or work transfer is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
